project.name: MCP-alpaca v1
project.description: Multi-exchange crypto/stock range-trading bot system with Alpaca paper, Kraken spot live, Bitvavo EUR, and Hybrid regime trader sharing common infrastructure.

nodes.name: live_trader.py
nodes.summary: Main Alpaca paper trading entry point implementing hourly range-based crypto buy/sell logic, symbol selection, and order lifecycle via run_once and main.

nodes.name: strategy_core.py
nodes.summary: Venue-neutral strategy core providing range-level scoring, spread filtering, and top-symbol selection logic shared by both Alpaca and Kraken bots.

nodes.name: cancel_all_orders.py
nodes.summary: Standalone utility script that cancels all open Alpaca orders, used for manual intervention or position resets.

nodes.name: config.py
nodes.summary: Central configuration hub reading environment variables for API keys, trading parameters, and shared constants used by all bots in the system.

nodes.name: run_audit.py
nodes.summary: Provides run-audit logging helpers that append JSONL records of each bot run for monitoring, comparison, and post-run analysis.

nodes.name: backtest.py
nodes.summary: Core range-strategy backtesting engine that fetches historical OHLCV data and simulates buy/sell range trades with P&L reporting.

nodes.name: backtest_all.py
nodes.summary: Batch backtest runner that iterates over all configured symbols and invokes the core backtest engine for each, aggregating results.

nodes.name: kraken_runtime.py
nodes.summary: Kraken spot USD runtime providing ccxt exchange connectivity, order submission, position tracking, state persistence, fill detection, and Telegram notifications.

nodes.name: live_trader.py
nodes.summary: Kraken live trading entry point implementing hourly range strategy execution with symbol selection, order lifecycle management, and dry-run support.

nodes.name: test_strategy_core.py
nodes.summary: Pytest test suite for strategy_core.py verifying level scoring, spread filtering, and top-symbol selection logic with unit tests.

nodes.name: _fetch_alpaca_daily_rows
nodes.summary: Fetches recent daily OHLCV bars from Alpaca crypto data client and returns structured row dicts per symbol.

nodes.name: get_24h_levels
nodes.summary: Returns range levels derived from last 24h bars for symbols that pass the minimum spread filter.

nodes.name: _get_levels_and_scores
nodes.summary: Combines data fetch and level scoring into a single scored-levels map for all pool symbols.

nodes.name: select_top_symbols
nodes.summary: Selects top N tradeable symbols by score, respecting current positions and minimum spread constraints.

nodes.name: _order_age_hours
nodes.summary: Calculates the age of an Alpaca order in hours from its created_at timestamp, handling timezone-aware and naive datetimes.

nodes.name: run_once
nodes.summary: Core trading cycle executing symbol selection, position evaluation, order placement/cancellation, and sell/buy logic with Telegram notifications and run-audit logging.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Entry point that runs the hourly trading loop, handling exceptions and sleeping between cycles.

nodes.name: levels_score_from_daily_rows
nodes.summary: Computes high/low range levels and a quality score from a list of daily OHLCV rows for a single symbol.

nodes.name: levels_passing_spread
nodes.summary: Returns range levels only if the spread exceeds the configured minimum fraction threshold, otherwise returns None.

nodes.name: build_levels_scored_from_symbol_rows
nodes.summary: Builds a dict mapping symbol to scored range levels from a symbol-keyed rows map, skipping symbols with insufficient data.

nodes.name: select_top_symbols_from_scores
nodes.summary: Selects the top N symbols by level score while preserving currently held position symbols up to the cap.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Initializes Alpaca trading client and cancels all open orders, logging each cancellation result.

nodes.name: required_min_spread_fraction_crypto_usd
nodes.summary: Returns the minimum required spread fraction for a given crypto/USD pair based on configured per-symbol thresholds.

nodes.name: log_run_audit
nodes.summary: Appends a structured run-audit entry to a per-bot JSONL file recording run metadata for comparison.

nodes.name: load_run_audits
nodes.summary: Loads and parses run-audit records from a JSONL file for post-run analysis and comparison reporting.

nodes.name: fetch_data
nodes.summary: Fetches historical OHLCV data for a given symbol and date range from the configured data source.

nodes.name: run_backtest
nodes.summary: Simulates range-trading strategy on historical data, tracking buy/sell trades and computing detailed P&L metrics.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Backtest CLI entry point that parses arguments, runs the simulation, and prints performance results.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Runs backtests across all configured symbols sequentially and aggregates the results.

nodes.name: make_exchange
nodes.summary: Creates and configures a ccxt Kraken exchange instance with API credentials and rate-limit settings.

nodes.name: filter_kraken_usd_pool
nodes.summary: Filters the configured symbol pool to only USD-quoted pairs that are actively available on Kraken.

nodes.name: fetch_daily_rows_ccxt
nodes.summary: Fetches recent daily OHLCV bars via ccxt and returns structured row dicts suitable for strategy scoring.

nodes.name: fetch_symbol_rows_for_pool
nodes.summary: Fetches daily rows for all symbols in the pool, returning a map from symbol to row list.

nodes.name: get_buying_power_usd
nodes.summary: Returns available USD buying power from the Kraken account balance.

nodes.name: estimate_portfolio_usd
nodes.summary: Estimates total portfolio value in USD by pricing all held crypto positions at current mid prices.

nodes.name: get_positions_map
nodes.summary: Returns a map of symbol to held quantity for all non-USD positions currently held in the Kraken account.

nodes.name: submit_limit_buy
nodes.summary: Places a limit buy order on Kraken with optional post-only flag and dry-run support.

nodes.name: submit_limit_sell_all_free
nodes.summary: Places a limit sell order for the full free (unencumbered) position quantity at the target price.

nodes.name: get_mid_price
nodes.summary: Returns the mid-price (average of best bid and ask) for a symbol fetched from the order book.

nodes.name: _load_state
nodes.summary: Loads persisted Kraken trade state from JSON file, initializing default structure if the file is missing.

nodes.name: save_kraken_state
nodes.summary: Persists the Kraken trade state dict to a JSON file atomically.

nodes.name: append_kraken_fill_audit
nodes.summary: Appends a fill audit entry to the Kraken trade JSONL log for reconciliation.

nodes.name: check_and_notify_kraken_fills
nodes.summary: Detects filled Kraken orders by comparing ledger history, logs fills to JSONL, updates trade state, and sends Telegram notifications.

nodes.name: persist_entries_from_balances
nodes.summary: Persists account balance snapshot entries to the journal for reconciliation and portfolio tracking.

nodes.name: select_top_symbols_kraken
nodes.summary: Selects top range-trading symbols for Kraken by fetching ccxt OHLCV data and applying shared strategy scoring logic.

nodes.name: run_once
nodes.summary: Core Kraken trading cycle: checks fills, evaluates positions, places/cancels orders, and executes buy/sell decisions with comprehensive error handling.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Entry point for Kraken live trader that runs the hourly trading loop with exception handling and sleep between cycles.

nodes.name: test_select_top_symbols_keeps_positions_and_respects_cap_n
nodes.summary: Verifies that select_top_symbols_from_scores retains current position symbols and enforces the maximum cap N.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Empty package initializer that marks bot_hybrid as a Python package.

nodes.name: backtest_hybrid.py
nodes.summary: Standalone backtesting harness for the hybrid regime-trader; fetches historical hourly crypto bars, simulates range and trend strategies across symbols, and prints per-symbol and aggregate performance metrics (Sharpe, drawdown, win rate).

nodes.name: SymbolResult
nodes.summary: Dataclass holding backtest results for a single symbol/mode run, with computed properties for return percentage, win rate, max drawdown, and Sharpe ratio.

nodes.name: fetch_hourly_data
nodes.summary: Fetches hourly OHLCV crypto bars from Alpaca's historical data API for a list of symbols over a given number of months.

nodes.name: run_backtest
nodes.summary: Runs a full event-driven backtest simulation on a single symbol's DataFrame, applying regime detection and range/trend/hybrid signals to simulate trade entries, exits, trailing stops, and equity curve evolution.

nodes.name: _format_row
nodes.summary: Aggregates a list of SymbolResult objects into a formatted summary row with portfolio-level Sharpe, drawdown, and trade statistics.

nodes.name: _print_mode_results
nodes.summary: Prints per-symbol and aggregate performance tables for a given strategy mode to stdout.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry point that parses arguments, fetches data, runs backtests across all symbol/mode combinations, and prints results.

nodes.name: hybrid_trader.py
nodes.summary: Main live-trading entry point for the hourly hybrid regime-trader; orchestrates regime detection, signal generation, Alpaca order submission, state persistence, and Telegram notifications.

nodes.name: _load_hybrid_state
nodes.summary: Loads the hybrid trader's persisted JSON state (regime history and trend trade records) from disk, returning a default dict if not found.

nodes.name: _save_hybrid_state
nodes.summary: Atomically writes regime snapshots and trend-trade records to the hybrid state JSON file using a temp-file rename pattern.

nodes.name: fetch_hourly_bars
nodes.summary: Fetches the most recent N hourly OHLCV bars for a list of crypto symbols from Alpaca's data client.

nodes.name: _submit_limit_buy
nodes.summary: Submits a limit buy order to Alpaca's trading client for a given symbol, quantity, and price.

nodes.name: _execute_signal
nodes.summary: Translates a StrategySignal into live Alpaca orders: cancels conflicting open orders, submits limit buys or sells, and handles trailing-stop exits for both range and trend positions.

nodes.name: _log_regime_line
nodes.summary: Emits a structured log line recording the current regime snapshot, active strategy, and execution status for a symbol.

nodes.name: run_once
nodes.summary: Core hourly execution loop: fetches bars and account state, detects market regimes, generates hybrid signals via pick_hybrid_signal, executes orders through Alpaca, and persists updated state.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Process entry point that logs startup configuration and runs the run_once loop on a configurable schedule with retry/sleep between iterations.

nodes.name: indicators.py
nodes.summary: Pure NumPy/Pandas technical indicator library providing EMA, True Range, ATR, and ADX (with +DI/-DI) calculations used by the regime detector and strategy modules.

nodes.name: ema
nodes.summary: Computes exponential moving average of a Pandas Series using a given span period.

nodes.name: true_range
nodes.summary: Computes the Wilder true range series from an OHLCV DataFrame as the max of three absolute differences.

nodes.name: atr
nodes.summary: Computes Average True Range by applying Wilder smoothing to the true range series.

nodes.name: adx
nodes.summary: Computes the ADX, +DI, and -DI directional movement indicators using Wilder smoothing; returns a DataFrame with all three series.

nodes.name: market_regime_detector.py
nodes.summary: Classifies market regime as 'trend' or 'range' based on ADX and EMA crossover analysis with hysteresis confirmation, and provides state persistence for regime history.

nodes.name: RegimeSnapshot
nodes.summary: Dataclass capturing a full regime classification result: current/previous regime, ADX values, EMA levels, close price, and human-readable reason string.

nodes.name: detect_regime
nodes.summary: Analyzes recent hourly bars to determine whether the market is in a trend or range regime using ADX thresholds, EMA crossover direction, and confirmation bars with hysteresis.

nodes.name: load_regime_state
nodes.summary: Loads the persisted regime state dict from a JSON file, returning an empty dict if the file does not exist.

nodes.name: save_regime_state
nodes.summary: Atomically merges new regime snapshots into the persisted state JSON using a temp-file rename pattern.

nodes.name: range_strategy.py
nodes.summary: Mean-reversion range strategy that computes hourly support/resistance levels from ATR and price history, then generates buy/sell/hold signals with risk-managed sizing.

nodes.name: _hybrid_mr_min_spread_pct
nodes.summary: Calculates the minimum spread percentage required for a valid range trade based on ATR and configurable thresholds from context.

nodes.name: compute_hourly_levels
nodes.summary: Computes support and resistance levels and ATR from a rolling window of hourly bars.

nodes.name: generate_signal
nodes.summary: Generates a StrategySignal (BUY, SELL, or HOLD) for the range regime by comparing current price to computed support/resistance levels with minimum spread and risk constraints.

nodes.name: risk_manager.py
nodes.summary: Position sizing and stop-loss profile calculations for range and trend strategies, implementing fixed-fraction risk-per-trade with ATR-based stop and take-profit levels.

nodes.name: StopProfile
nodes.summary: Dataclass holding a trade's computed stop price, take-profit level, and trailing percentage, with a describe() method for log formatting.

nodes.name: position_size
nodes.summary: Calculates the number of units to buy given equity, entry/stop prices, a risk percentage, and an optional capital cap using fixed-fraction position sizing.

nodes.name: range_stop_profile
nodes.summary: Returns a StopProfile for a range trade with an ATR-based stop and a sell-level take-profit.

nodes.name: trend_stop_profile
nodes.summary: Returns a StopProfile for a trend trade with an ATR-based initial stop and a trailing percentage.

nodes.name: trailing_stop_price
nodes.summary: Computes the current trailing stop price from the highest close since entry and a trailing percentage.

nodes.name: strategy_base.py
nodes.summary: Defines the shared StrategyContext and StrategySignal dataclasses used across all hybrid sub-strategies as the common interface for inputs and outputs.

nodes.name: StrategyContext
nodes.summary: Dataclass carrying the per-symbol market context (price, equity, position state) passed into each strategy's generate_signal call.

nodes.name: StrategySignal
nodes.summary: Dataclass representing a strategy decision (BUY/SELL/HOLD) with associated price targets, stop, quantity, and trailing percentage; includes as_log_line() for structured logging.

nodes.name: trend_strategy.py
nodes.summary: EMA-crossover trend-following strategy that generates entry/exit signals based on golden/death crosses, ADX trend strength, and trailing stop management.

nodes.name: _recent_golden_cross
nodes.summary: Detects whether a golden cross (fast EMA crossing above slow EMA) occurred within the recent lookback window.

nodes.name: generate_signal
nodes.summary: Generates a StrategySignal for the trend regime using EMA crossovers, ADX confirmation, trailing-stop exits, and ATR-based position sizing.

nodes.name: hybrid_signals.py
nodes.summary: Bridge module that routes to the correct sub-strategy's generate_signal based on the current regime snapshot, implementing the hybrid signal selection logic used by the live trader.

nodes.name: pick_hybrid_signal
nodes.summary: Selects and returns a StrategySignal by dispatching to range or trend strategy based on the current RegimeSnapshot, with transitional regime handling.

nodes.name: alpaca_runtime.py
nodes.summary: Core Alpaca trading runtime shared by the range and hybrid bots: initialises TradingClient/DataClient, fetches prices, positions, and orders, submits crypto limit-sells, and manages trade state with deduplication-based order-fill notifications via Telegram.
nodes.languageNotes: Heavy use of Decimal arithmetic for precise crypto quantity handling alongside Alpaca SDK Pydantic models.

nodes.name: daily_report.py
nodes.summary: Generates and sends a daily P&L Telegram report by comparing the current portfolio value with the saved day-start value, including cumulative fictive fee tracking.

nodes.name: export_alpaca_orders.py
nodes.summary: CLI tool that fetches filled Alpaca orders for a configurable date range, deduplicates them, and writes per-symbol CSVs, a JSON summary, and a Markdown report to the output directory.

nodes.name: run_loop.py
nodes.summary: Main hourly orchestration loop: initialises the day-start snapshot, invokes the range-trading run_once step each hour, triggers a daily report at midnight, and sends Telegram status messages.

nodes.name: status.py
nodes.summary: CLI diagnostic script that prints current Alpaca account state including buying power, portfolio value, open positions, live prices, and pending orders for each tracked symbol.

nodes.name: telegram.py
nodes.summary: Telegram notification service that sends plain messages and rich trade-fill summaries (P&L, fee breakdown, portfolio snapshot) to the configured chat via the Bot API, with a urllib fallback.

nodes.name: test_telegram.py
nodes.summary: Manual smoke-test script that exercises the Telegram notification functions with hardcoded test values to verify bot token and chat-id configuration.

nodes.name: live_trader.py
nodes.summary: Thin compatibility shim that re-exports everything from alpaca_bot.live_trader, allowing bot_range_1000 importers to use the module path without duplicating logic.

nodes.name: _alpaca_bot_trade_log_path
nodes.summary: Resolves the path for the Alpaca fill-audit JSONL log file from environment variable ALPACA_BOT_TRADE_LOG, expanding user home and handling relative paths relative to the project root.

nodes.name: _order_audit_snapshot
nodes.summary: Serialises an Alpaca order object to a flat dictionary suitable for JSONL audit logging, normalising datetime fields to ISO strings.

nodes.name: append_alpaca_bot_fill_audit
nodes.summary: Appends a single fill-audit record as a JSON line to the configured trade-log file, creating parent directories as needed.

nodes.name: get_trading_clients
nodes.summary: Constructs and returns an (TradingClient, CryptoHistoricalDataClient) tuple from ALPACA_API_KEY / ALPACA_SECRET_KEY environment variables, respecting the ALPACA_PAPER_TRADE flag.

nodes.name: get_current_prices
nodes.summary: Fetches the latest bid/ask midpoint prices for a list of crypto symbols using CryptoLatestQuoteRequest, returning a symbol-to-price mapping.

nodes.name: _decimal_from_json_qty
nodes.summary: Safely converts a raw quantity value from an Alpaca JSON model dump (str, int, float, or Decimal) to a Python Decimal for precise arithmetic.

nodes.name: _sell_qty_decimal_from_position
nodes.summary: Determines the correct Decimal quantity to sell from a position object, preferring available quantity over total quantity to avoid over-selling.

nodes.name: _submit_crypto_sell
nodes.summary: Submits a limit sell order for a crypto position via the Alpaca TradingClient, deriving quantity from the position object and rounding the limit price.

nodes.name: _parse_order_ts
nodes.summary: Parses an Alpaca order timestamp field (datetime object or ISO string) to a timezone-aware datetime, returning datetime.min on parse failure.

nodes.name: _load_state
nodes.summary: Reads the persistent trade-state JSON file (.alpaca_trade_state.json), returning a dict with cost entries, notified order IDs, and cumulative fictive fees.

nodes.name: _save_state
nodes.summary: Persists the trade-state dict (entries, notified IDs, cumulative fees) atomically to .alpaca_trade_state.json, merging with any existing state.

nodes.name: _known_notified_order_ids
nodes.summary: Builds the deduplicated set of order IDs that have already been notified by combining the in-memory state and the persistent JSONL fill-audit log.

nodes.name: _apply_buy_to_entries
nodes.summary: Updates the cost-basis entries dict for a buy fill using a weighted-average entry price calculation.

nodes.name: _check_and_notify_filled_orders
nodes.summary: Core hourly routine that fetches recent filled orders from Alpaca, deduplicates against known IDs, computes P&L and fees for each new fill, logs to journal, and dispatches Telegram fill notifications before persisting updated state.

nodes.name: send_daily_report
nodes.summary: Computes the day's P&L by comparing current portfolio value with the saved day-start value and sends a formatted Telegram summary including cumulative fee totals.

nodes.name: _utc_range_inclusive
nodes.summary: Converts an inclusive start/end date pair to a UTC datetime half-open interval [lo, hi_exclusive) suitable for the Alpaca orders query.

nodes.name: fetch_filled_orders
nodes.summary: Pages through Alpaca filled orders within a time window, deduplicates by ID, filters by symbol, and returns a sorted list of order objects.

nodes.name: _order_to_row
nodes.summary: Converts an Alpaca order object to a flat CSV-ready dict with normalised timestamps, side, symbol, qty, price, and notional value.

nodes.name: _write_summary_md
nodes.summary: Writes a Markdown summary file with export metadata, buy/sell counts, and per-symbol cost basis from the export run.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry point for the order export tool: parses date/symbol arguments, fetches and formats filled orders, and writes CSV, JSON, and Markdown output files.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Hourly run loop: calls get_trading_clients, triggers run_once for the range strategy, sends Telegram heartbeats, fires the daily report at midnight, and sleeps until the next hour.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Prints a diagnostic status table for each tracked symbol: buying power, portfolio value, positions, current prices, and open limit orders.

nodes.name: send_telegram
nodes.summary: Sends a plain-text Telegram message using the Bot API via requests (with urllib fallback), reading token and chat ID from environment variables.

nodes.name: notify_trade_filled
nodes.summary: Builds and sends a rich Telegram fill notification with P&L, cost basis, estimated fees (buy/sell rates, fixed per-fill, optional EUR fee), and current portfolio value.

nodes.name: bitvavo_config.py
nodes.summary: Defines Bitvavo trading configuration constants (symbols pool, order sizing, spread thresholds) and a helper to compute the minimum required spread fraction based on notional size.

nodes.name: bitvavo_daily_report.py
nodes.summary: Generates and sends a daily performance report for the Bitvavo EUR portfolio by comparing current portfolio value against the saved day-start snapshot via Telegram.

nodes.name: bitvavo_trader.py
nodes.summary: Core Bitvavo EUR spot trading bot using ccxt; implements the full range-trading loop including symbol selection, order placement and cancellation, fill detection, JSONL journaling, Telegram notifications, and run auditing.
nodes.languageNotes: Single-file module acting as both library (exported helpers) and runnable entry point via the `main` loop.

nodes.name: journal.py
nodes.summary: Provides JSONL-based trade journaling for the entire bot system: appends filled trade records and exposes `load_trades` and `known_order_ids` for deduplication across restarts.

nodes.name: report.py
nodes.summary: Reads the trade journal and computes a configurable portfolio performance report (P&L, win rate, per-symbol breakdown), then prints and optionally sends it via Telegram.

nodes.name: test_journal_dedupe.py
nodes.summary: Pytest test that verifies `known_order_ids` correctly reads the JSONL journal for deduplication and ignores corrupt/extra lines.

nodes.name: required_min_spread_fraction
nodes.summary: Returns the minimum required bid-ask spread fraction for a trade given a reference notional EUR amount, scaling dynamically with order size.

nodes.name: load_day_start
nodes.summary: Loads the persisted day-start portfolio snapshot from disk, returning the saved timestamp and EUR value.

nodes.name: send_daily_report
nodes.summary: Fetches current portfolio value, computes P&L against the day-start snapshot, formats a Telegram message, sends it, and saves a new day-start baseline.

nodes.name: get_exchange
nodes.summary: Initialises and returns a configured ccxt Bitvavo exchange instance, reading API credentials from environment variables and loading markets.

nodes.name: get_balance
nodes.summary: Returns the free EUR cash balance from the Bitvavo account.

nodes.name: get_portfolio_value
nodes.summary: Computes total EUR portfolio value by fetching all balances and converting non-EUR holdings to EUR using live ticker prices.

nodes.name: _trade_fee_in_eur
nodes.summary: Calculates the total trade fee in EUR for a given fill, handling multi-currency fee structures by fetching live conversion rates when needed.

nodes.name: get_current_prices
nodes.summary: Fetches and returns a dict of current bid/ask/last prices for a list of symbols from Bitvavo.

nodes.name: get_24h_levels
nodes.summary: Computes 24-hour high/low/average price levels from OHLCV data for each given symbol to determine range bounds.

nodes.name: _get_levels_and_scores
nodes.summary: Fetches OHLCV data and computes range-based opportunity scores (spread relative to min spread fraction) used to rank symbols.

nodes.name: get_positions
nodes.summary: Returns a dict of currently held base-asset quantities for the requested symbols by reading the exchange balance.

nodes.name: select_top_symbols
nodes.summary: Scores all candidate symbols against the range strategy criteria and returns the top N selected for trading, prioritising symbols already in the portfolio.

nodes.name: get_bot_open_orders
nodes.summary: Retrieves currently open orders placed by the bot for a given symbol, filtering by known bot order IDs.

nodes.name: _order_size_ok
nodes.summary: Validates that a proposed order quantity and price meet the exchange's minimum cost and amount limits before submission.

nodes.name: _load_state
nodes.summary: Loads the persisted bot trading state (entry prices, notified order IDs, open bot orders) from a JSON file on disk.

nodes.name: _save_state
nodes.summary: Persists updated bot trading state to disk, merging new entries with existing state to avoid data loss between runs.

nodes.name: _check_and_notify_filled_trades
nodes.summary: Polls the exchange for recent fills, deduplicates against the JSONL journal, computes P&L and fees, logs each new fill, and sends Telegram fill notifications.

nodes.name: run_once
nodes.summary: Executes one full trading iteration: checks fills, evaluates open orders (cancelling stale/drifted ones), places new buy/sell limit orders for selected symbols, and emits a status Telegram message.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Entry-point loop that runs `run_once` repeatedly with a configurable sleep interval, logging startup parameters and handling exceptions gracefully.

nodes.name: log_trade
nodes.summary: Appends a completed trade record to the JSONL journal file, enriching the raw fill with computed P&L, fee, portfolio value, and timestamp fields.

nodes.name: known_order_ids
nodes.summary: Returns a frozenset of all order IDs already present in the JSONL journal, used to deduplicate fill notifications across bot restarts.

nodes.name: load_trades
nodes.summary: Reads and parses all trade records from the JSONL journal file, skipping malformed lines, and returns them as a list of dicts.

nodes.name: _parse_args
nodes.summary: Parses command-line arguments to configure the report's lookback window (days) and whether to include all trades or only recent ones.

nodes.name: build_report
nodes.summary: Aggregates trade journal records into a structured report dict with P&L totals, win/loss counts, per-symbol breakdown, and best/worst trades.

nodes.name: format_report
nodes.summary: Converts a report dict into a human-readable multi-line string suitable for printing or Telegram delivery.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry point that builds, formats, prints, and optionally sends the portfolio report via Telegram.

nodes.name: test_known_order_ids_reads_journal
nodes.summary: Verifies that `known_order_ids` correctly reads previously logged order IDs from the JSONL journal and returns an empty frozenset when no prior trades exist.

nodes.name: __main__.py
nodes.summary: Package entry point that delegates to the CLI main function, enabling `python -m metrics.bitvavo_compare` invocation.

nodes.name: cli.py
nodes.summary: Argparse-based CLI for the bitvavo_compare tool, providing `journal-export` and `metrics` subcommands that orchestrate journal normalization and metrics summary generation.

nodes.name: journal_normalize.py
nodes.summary: Core normalization library that loads Bitvavo JSONL trade journals, deduplicates and filters trades by date range, and writes them to normalized CSV format.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses datetime timezone-aware parsing with fromisoformat and manual UTC coercion; merge_bitvavo_only is the main pipeline combining multiple JSONL sources.

nodes.name: metrics_summary.py
nodes.summary: Computes per-symbol buy/sell trade metrics from normalized CSV rows and formats results as a Markdown summary table.

nodes.name: export_bitvavo_trades.py
nodes.summary: Standalone CLI script that merges and exports Bitvavo trade data from JSONL journals to both JSON and CSV output files.

nodes.name: cmd_journal_export
nodes.summary: Handles the `journal-export` subcommand by resolving paths, invoking merge_bitvavo_only, and writing the resulting rows to a CSV file.

nodes.name: cmd_metrics
nodes.summary: Handles the `metrics` subcommand by loading rows from multiple CSV files, summarizing each, formatting the combined result as Markdown, and writing to an output file.

nodes.name: build_parser
nodes.summary: Constructs and returns the argparse ArgumentParser with all subcommands, arguments, and defaults for the bitvavo_compare CLI.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Entry point that builds the argument parser, parses argv, and dispatches to the appropriate subcommand handler.

nodes.name: parse_instant_utc
nodes.summary: Parses an ISO-8601 datetime string into a UTC-aware datetime object, handling strings with and without timezone suffixes.

nodes.name: parse_range
nodes.summary: Parses start/end date strings into a UTC-aware datetime range tuple, accepting both date-only and full ISO datetime formats.

nodes.name: load_jsonl
nodes.summary: Reads a JSONL file line by line and returns a list of parsed dictionaries, returning an empty list if the file does not exist.

nodes.name: row_to_normalized
nodes.summary: Transforms a raw Bitvavo trade record dict into a normalized flat dict with standardized field names and quote/base asset classification.

nodes.name: write_csv
nodes.summary: Writes a list of normalized row dicts to a CSV file with a fixed set of column headers, creating parent directories as needed.

nodes.name: merge_bitvavo_only
nodes.summary: Merges multiple Bitvavo JSONL sources, deduplicates by order-id+side, filters by date range and EUR quote currency, and returns normalized trade rows.

nodes.name: load_rows

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README and the comprehensive architecture doc to understand what this project is: a multi-exchange crypto/stock range-trading system running on Alpaca (paper), Kraken (spot USD live), Bitvavo (EUR live), and a hybrid regime-trader — all triggered hourly by GitHub Actions. The README is intentionally minimal, but CODEBASE_CONTEXT_FOR_V2.md is the definitive internal reference covering every module, design decision, and data flow. Reading both before any code gives you the conceptual map that makes every subsequent file immediately legible.

tour.title: Environment & Configuration
tour.description: Before any bot can run, it needs API keys, exchange secrets, and trading parameters. The `.env.example` file is the complete inventory of every secret the system requires — Alpaca, Kraken, Bitvavo, and Telegram credentials all live here as environment variables. `bot_live/config.py` is the highest-fanin file in the entire codebase (imported by 8 modules): it reads these environment variables at import time and exposes typed constants that every bot, runtime, and utility consumes, making it the single source of truth for system-wide settings.
tour.languageLesson: Python reads environment variables at module import time via os.getenv(). Using a single config.py as a central hub prevents scattered os.getenv() calls and makes it easy to audit what settings exist and what their defaults are.

tour.title: Notifications & Trade Journal
tour.description: Two shared services form the observability backbone used by every bot in the system. `telegram.py` sends real-time alerts — plain status messages during a run, and rich trade-fill summaries with P&L breakdown and portfolio snapshot when an order fills. `journal.py` is the JSONL trade ledger: it provides `log_trade`, `load_trades`, and `known_order_ids` — the last function being critical for deduplication so the same fill is never double-counted across hourly runs or bot restarts. Both modules are imported by Alpaca, Kraken, and Bitvavo runtimes.
tour.languageLesson: JSONL (JSON Lines) appends one JSON object per line, making it safe for concurrent writers and trivial to stream-process. Unlike a full JSON array, appending a new trade never requires rewriting the entire file.

tour.title: Alpaca Trading Runtime
tour.description: The `alpaca_runtime.py` is the core Alpaca exchange layer, shared by both the range bot and the hybrid bot. It initialises the Alpaca `TradingClient` and `DataClient`, fetches live prices and current positions, submits crypto limit-sell orders, and manages a persistent `.alpaca_trade_state.json` file for cross-run deduplication. On each invocation it checks for newly filled orders by diffing known order IDs against live fills, then fires rich Telegram notifications. Understanding this file is essential before looking at either Alpaca-connected entry point.

tour.title: Venue-Neutral Range Strategy
tour.description: The range trading philosophy of the system is entirely encoded in `strategy_core.py` — and by design it knows nothing about Alpaca or Kraken. It takes price data and produces range-level scores, filters symbols by spread quality, and returns the top candidates to trade. Both `alpaca_bot/live_trader.py` and `kraken/live_trader.py` import this same module, so any strategy improvement automatically applies to both venues. This separation is the key architectural decision that keeps strategy logic clean and venue logic confined to the runtimes.
tour.languageLesson: Venue-neutral strategy modules are a form of dependency inversion: the strategy doesn't call exchange APIs; instead, callers pass in price data and receive signals. This makes the strategy independently testable, as shown by tests/test_strategy_core.py.

tour.title: Alpaca Range Bot Entry Points
tour.description: `alpaca_bot/live_trader.py` is the concrete Alpaca range-trading runner — it wires together `strategy_core`, `alpaca_runtime`, `config`, and `telegram` into a single `run_once()` function that executes one hourly trading cycle: select symbols, evaluate range levels, submit limit orders, and log results. `bot_live/run_loop.py` is the long-running process wrapper that calls `run_once()` on the hour, initialises a daily snapshot at day-start, and fires a midnight report — this is what would run if you deployed the bot as a persistent process rather than via GitHub Actions.

tour.title: Kraken Spot Bot
tour.description: The Kraken bot mirrors the Alpaca range bot but targets real USD spot markets via the ccxt library. `kraken_runtime.py` is the Kraken-specific exchange layer: ccxt connectivity, order submission, position tracking, its own `.kraken_trade_state.json`, fill detection, and Telegram notifications — all parallel to `alpaca_runtime.py` but self-contained. `kraken/live_trader.py` is the entry point that reuses the shared `strategy_core.py` for signal generation, demonstrating how the venue-neutral strategy pattern makes adding a new exchange a matter of writing just a new runtime and entry point.

tour.title: Technical Indicators
tour.description: The hybrid bot requires a richer set of technical indicators than simple range levels. `indicators.py` is a pure NumPy/Pandas library computing EMA, True Range, ATR, and ADX — it has no side effects, no exchange calls, and no state, making it the safest and most reusable module in the codebase (fanIn: 3, used by range_strategy, trend_strategy, and market_regime_detector). `strategy_base.py` defines the `StrategyContext` and `StrategySignal` dataclasses that all hybrid sub-strategies use as their shared interface — the contract that allows the regime detector to dispatch to any sub-strategy without knowing its internals.
tour.languageLesson: Python dataclasses (introduced in 3.7) generate __init__, __repr__, and __eq__ automatically from field annotations. Using them as strategy I/O types makes function signatures self-documenting and easy to test without mocking.

tour.title: Hybrid Regime Detection
tour.description: The insight behind the hybrid bot is that different market conditions call for different strategies — and `market_regime_detector.py` makes that determination automatically. It computes ADX (from `indicators.py`) and EMA crossovers on recent hourly price bars, then classifies the market as either 'trend' or 'range' with hysteresis to avoid rapid regime flipping. The output of this module drives the dispatch in `hybrid_signals.py` (Step 11), routing signals to the appropriate sub-strategy. This is the decision brain of the entire hybrid system.
tour.languageLesson: Hysteresis in regime detection means the classifier requires the new regime signal to persist for multiple bars before switching, preventing costly strategy whipsaw in ambiguous markets. This is a common pattern in technical trading systems.

tour.title: Hybrid Sub-Strategies & Risk
tour.description: With regime detection in place, the system needs a strategy for each regime. `range_strategy.py` implements mean-reversion using hourly ATR-based support/resistance levels, generating buy/sell/hold signals when price is near range extremes. `trend_strategy.py` implements EMA crossover trend-following, generating signals on golden/death crosses filtered by ADX strength. Both conform to the `StrategyContext`/`StrategySignal` interface from Step 8. `risk_manager.py` sits alongside them, translating signals into position sizes and stop-loss levels appropriate for each regime — range positions are sized tighter than trend positions.

tour.title: Hybrid Bot Entry Point
tour.description: `bot_live/hybrid_signals.py` is the bridge: given the current regime from `market_regime_detector.py`, it routes the `generate_signal` call to either `range_strategy` or `trend_strategy`, returning a unified `StrategySignal`. `bot_hybrid/hybrid_trader.py` is the top-level entry point that orchestrates everything each hour: fetch prices, detect regime, generate signal via `hybrid_signals`, size the position via `risk_manager`, submit orders via `alpaca_runtime`, persist state, and notify via Telegram. This file is the highest fan-out node in the hybrid layer, pulling together every module in the hybrid stack.

tour.title: Bitvavo EUR Bot
tour.description: The Bitvavo bot trades EUR-denominated crypto on the Bitvavo exchange using ccxt, making it the third independent venue in the system. `bitvavo_trader.py` is a self-contained module that handles the full order lifecycle — exchange initialisation, order submission, fill detection, state persistence, and Telegram notifications — all in one file, unlike the Alpaca bot which splits runtime and entry point across modules. It shares `config.py`, `journal.py`, and `telegram.py` with the rest of the system but has its own ccxt client and EUR-specific order logic.

tour.title: Backtesting & Tests
tour.description: Before deploying a range strategy live, it can be validated offline with `bot_range_1000/backtest.py` — a simulation engine that replays historical price data, simulates the buy/sell logic, and produces P&L reports. The `tests/` directory adds fast unit coverage: `test_strategy_core.py` verifies range-level scoring, spread filtering, and top-symbol selection directly against `strategy_core.py`, while `test_journal_dedupe.py` validates that `known_order_ids` correctly deduplicates across sessions. These tests serve as both regression guards and living documentation of expected strategy behaviour.
tour.languageLesson: Pytest's parametrize decorator lets a single test function cover many input/output cases without code duplication. Testing the strategy core in isolation (without exchange connectivity) keeps tests fast and deterministic.

tour.title: Trade Data & Reporting
tour.description: The system accumulates a durable trade history through `export_trade_log.py`, which merges per-run JSONL files into the persistent `data/alpaca_trades.jsonl` committed to the repository by CI — creating a git-backed trade ledger that survives process restarts. `run_audit.py` appends a structured record after every bot run (exit code, positions, elapsed time) to per-bot audit JSONL files, enabling health monitoring. The `metrics/` modules then analyse this data: `metrics/run_compare/load_export.py` computes bot health statistics across venues, and `metrics/bitvavo_compare/cli.py` provides per-symbol performance comparison for Bitvavo.

tour.title: CI/CD Pipelines
tour.description: The entire system runs serverlessly on GitHub Actions with no always-on infrastructure. Three separate workflows drive the three live venues: `trade.yml` triggers `alpaca_bot/live_trader.py` on the hour and exports the updated trade log back to the repo; `trade_v2.yml` runs the hybrid trader; and `trade_bitvavo.yml` runs the Bitvavo bot. Each workflow injects secrets (API keys, Telegram token) as environment variables at runtime, which `config.py` reads at import time — completing the loop back to Step 2. This design means the entire trading infrastructure is version-controlled, auditable, and requires zero server management.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions `schedule: cron` triggers run on UTC time. Each job runs in a fresh ephemeral container, so all persistent state must be read from and written back to the repository (via git commit in the workflow) or external storage — which is why the trade log export step exists in trade.yml.
